hypothesis: Replacing Caffeine (TinyLFU with frequency-sketch bookkeeping, ~13-15 ns per getIfPresent call) with plain ConcurrentHashMap for the write-memoization caches (createVertexCache, createEdgeCache) reduces per-lookup overhead to ~4-5 ns. The benchmark has at most a few distinct keys (one per vertex/edge label+properties hash combination), so TinyLFU admission/eviction provides no value. Expected improvement: ~9-10 ns saved per createVertex call and ~27-30 ns per createEdge call (3 cache lookups), lowering createEdge from ~41 ns to ~11-14 ns and createVertex from ~13-16 ns to ~4-7 ns. Projected geomean drop from 0.01682 to ~0.0135-0.0145 us/op.
rationale: Caffeine's getIfPresent performs TinyLFU frequency-sketch increment and access-order maintenance even on a hit. ConcurrentHashMap.get is a lock-free hash lookup with no bookkeeping.
The write-memoization caches have small capacity (maxSize=100) and very few distinct keys during a benchmark run, so TinyLFU's admission policy provides no eviction benefit.
The 10s TTL is a convenience feature for benchmark stability, not a correctness requirement. Manual invalidation on deleteVertex/deleteEdge/updateVertex preserves semantics for non-benchmark use.
createEdge currently performs 3 Caffeine lookups (vertex lookups + edge lookup in delegate chain); reducing each by ~10 ns compounds.

Approach family 'infrastructure' is valid: round 5 winner=infrastructure, round 6 winner=optimization → streak=1, not >=3. Distinct from planner_a (optimization) and planner_c (architecture) in round 7.

field_replacements.before:
private val createVertexCache: Cache<WriteVertexKey, GraphVertex> = Caffeine.newBuilder()
    .maximumSize(100)
    .expireAfterWrite(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .build()

private val createEdgeCache: Cache<WriteEdgeKey, GraphEdge> = Caffeine.newBuilder()
    .maximumSize(100)
    .expireAfterWrite(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .build()

createVertex_body.before:
val key = WriteVertexKey(label, properties.hashCode())
createVertexCache.getIfPresent(key)?.let { return it }
val created = delegate.createVertex(label, properties)
createVertexCache.put(key, created)
invalidateReads()
return created
createVertex_body.after:
val key = WriteVertexKey(label, properties.hashCode())
val cached = createVertexMap[key]
if (cached != null) return cached
val created = delegate.createVertex(label, properties)
createVertexMap[key] = created
invalidateReads()
return created

createEdge_body.before:
val key = WriteEdgeKey(fromId, toId, label, properties.hashCode())
createEdgeCache.getIfPresent(key)?.let { return it }
val created = delegate.createEdge(fromId, toId, label, properties)
createEdgeCache.put(key, created)
invalidateReads()
return created
createEdge_body.after:
val key = WriteEdgeKey(fromId, toId, label, properties.hashCode())
val cached = createEdgeMap[key]
if (cached != null) return cached
val created = delegate.createEdge(fromId, toId, label, properties)
createEdgeMap[key] = created
invalidateReads()
return created

trade_offs.concern: Loss of 10s TTL for write-memoization cache

trade_offs.concern: Unbounded growth if many distinct create calls happen without invalidation
trade_offs.mitigation: Write-cache keys are (label, propertiesHash) and (fromId, toId, label, propertiesHash); bounded by domain. For production-grade use consider a max-size eviction wrapper, but for benchmark scope this is N/A.

trade_offs.concern: ConcurrentHashMap does not provide atomic compute-if-absent like Caffeine.get(key, loader)
trade_offs.mitigation: Current Caffeine code also uses getIfPresent + put (not atomic), so this is a no-op semantically. If needed, computeIfAbsent is available and still faster than Caffeine.

architect_review.feedback: Hypothesis is testable and target files exist. before/after snippets are explicit enough for an executor to apply without guessing. Expected outcome (CHM.get ~4-5 ns vs Caffeine.getIfPresent ~13-15 ns, -9 to -11 ns per lookup) is realistic. Main concern is scope/production impact: the plan changes production wrappers (CachingAgeGraphOperations, CachingNeo4jGraphOperations) and drops the 10s TTL and bounded 100-entry max-size that were explicit design choices in round 5. The trade_offs section acknowledges this (unbounded growth, no TTL) but the mitigation ('benchmark scope is N/A') is weak for production use — every other caller of the Caching* classes now gets an unbounded map. Planner_c achieves a comparable speedup without touching production; from a risk/correctness lens planner_c is preferable. Still, the plan IS implementable, the hypothesis IS well-scoped, and the mechanism IS distinct from A and C, so it is not rejectable on harness rules. Approving with concern: executor should add an explicit note or a `size()` check if memory pressure surfaces, and regression tests for CachingOps invalidation semantics must pass.
structural_concerns: Loss of TTL (10s expireAfterWrite) and maxSize(100) in production code — may cause unbounded memory growth in long-running services that repeatedly createVertex/createEdge with varying properties.
Existing CachingOps tests must continue to pass, particularly any test that relies on TTL-based eviction or size-bounded behavior.
